original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.

actual_scope: At exactly 12 ordinary signed A_i/B_j queries for the fixed connected 3x3 signed target, extend the paid root alphabet from one-way transfers to either-direction arbitrary fixed nonzero Q/C elementary shears, both roots arbitrary dirty and restored. Prove the minimum four nonzero transfers; check a dimension-free <=3 monodromy reduction and replay the four-pass source word with all recursive children expanded.
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether a legally priced operation can favorably change recursive cost. The explicit reverse-direction root shear family is the changed operation. Its exact dirty-root monodromy shows no three-transfer saving; the four-transfer minimum carries the one-root obstruction through the source-connected matrix. No favorable completed budget or selected supplier is claimed.
bottleneck_link: Root-transfer passes are paid between complete recursive child queries. Ruling out any reduction from four to three under the expanded direction alphabet closes one proposed way to remove boundary work at the 12-child-query point. Port-weighted four-pass schedules and native adapters still need pricing, so this cannot improve the selected complex moment.
stop_rule: Price the optimistic delta of exactly one complete full-row transfer at fixed 12 queries. Stop when a written arbitrary-coefficient monodromy lemma excludes all <=3 restoring shears, the credited one-root 720-path census reproduces, and the exact four-pass predecessor word passes full noncommutative recursive replay plus controls. Bounded exact matrix domains: root counts 2,3,4; coefficients {-2,-1,1,2}; all 1-3 letter words, and 2-root four-letter controls. No coefficient/grid search beyond these finite controls.
evidence: verify.py independently replays 127,952 1-3 shear words for 2/3/4 roots, exact short-call event interleavings, all720 one-root paths, and the PR1651 four-pass word expanded to300 factor calls; see EVIDENCE.json and the universal written proof in README.md.

open_questions.blocked_by: No exact four-transfer bidirectional event classifier or port-specific native recursive tariff.
